findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC5's 'anywhere/without registration' promise with step 2's idiom-bounded coverage: either state that coverage is scoped to the enumerated bare-creation idioms (and that a genuinely new idiom shape requires extending the rule), or add a fallback that flags any -C target whose provenance the scan cannot resolve as a non-bare worktree.
evidence: AC5: 'adding a new bare-fixture test that uses git -C <bare> fails without any registration step'
Step 2: 'derive the identifiers bound to a bare repository from every --bare idiom actually present in this tree'
findings.finding: AC5 promises the guard catches 'adding a new bare-fixture test that uses git -C <bare> ... without any registration step', but step 2 derives bare-repo identifiers only from '--bare idiom[s] actually present in this tree' (last-path-operand, cwd-no-operand, and named factories). A new test that creates a bare repo via an idiom not among those enumerated would not be marked, so the -C would go undetected — the absolute AC phrasing overpromises relative to the idiom-bounded scan.
scenarios: A future test constructs a bare remote through a new helper shape not matching the enumerated idioms, uses git -C on it, and the guard stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scan sub-rule or note that any --bare-flagged git invocation whose bound identifier does not match a recognized non-bare shape is treated as bare (fail-closed), so novel bare-creation idioms are still marked rather than silently ignored.

findings.checklist_item: State the soundness boundary of the module-scoped-by-identifier marking (matches on identifier spelling, not dataflow) and either narrow the guard to the dataflow-backed idioms or explicitly accept and document the false-positive/false-negative envelope, so the footprint-file coverage does not silently depend on a name coincidence.
evidence: tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py:42-55: `_publish_ticket_store` runs `_git(remote.parent, "init", "--bare", str(remote))` on its PARAMETER `remote` but `return tracker` — the bare repo is never returned, so the caller's `remote = tmp_path / "origin.git"` at line 77 is marked only because the helper param and caller binding coincidentally share the name `remote`

Plan: 'Marking is otherwise module-scoped by identifier, which covers the same flow a second way when the caller reuses the helper's own name' — states the mechanism but not its failure modes (an unrelated worktree variable reusing a marked name is a false positive; a rename between helper param and caller binding not tracked via return is a false negative)
findings.finding: The Step-2 marking rule is module-scoped by identifier SPELLING, not dataflow, and this is load-bearing for the footprint file whose bare-repo binding is marked only by name coincidence (its creating helper _publish_ticket_store does not return the bare repo); the plan does not state the resulting false-positive/false-negative boundary.
findings.location: Plan Step 2 ('Marking is otherwise module-scoped by identifier') and Step 3 site count (footprint file, 4 sites)
scenarios: A future bare fixture whose helper param name differs from the caller's binding, with the helper not returning the repo, escapes the guard (a third recurrence — the exact failure mode this plan exists to prevent)
A worktree variable coincidentally named `remote` gets a `-C` call falsely flagged, forcing a spurious `_git_bare` conversion or a suppression

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.checklist_item: Justify why the new bare-repo `-C` detector cannot reuse the AST/argv/wrapper/marker primitives already in scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py (e.g. by extracting a shared module), or state the concrete divergence (WRITE-verb vs `-C`-discovery scope, src/scripts vs tests/ tree, gate vs pytest-oracle) that makes reuse infeasible.

check_raw_git_writes.py:462-467 `_wrapper_name` resolves a git wrapper called by name including attribute receivers (`core._git`, `self._git`) — the exact 'module-local helper that forwards its first parameter' shape the plan wants to detect
check_raw_git_writes.py:211-224 `_collect_markers` implements inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` sanction with mandatory reason — parallel to the plan's `-c safe.bareRepository=all` exemption

The plan text asserts 'scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py covers an unrelated concern' but does not consider factoring out its AST/argv/marker helpers for reuse
findings.finding: The proposed tree-derived AST detector rebuilds AST primitives that already exist in scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py (global-option-skipping git subcommand resolution via `_git_subcommand`, wrapper-name/attribute-receiver resolution via `WRAPPER_NAMES`+`_wrapper_name`, local argv/list tracking via `_resolve_argv`, and mandatory-reason inline-marker sanctioning via `_collect_markers`), yet the plan neither reuses nor references any of it.
scenarios: Author writes a bespoke `-C`-targeting resolver and re-derives global-option skipping, wrapper forwarding, and argv tracking that already exist and are already regression-tested
Two divergent AST git-command parsers now drift independently (e.g., a new git global option like `--config-env` handled in one but not the other)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to step 2 either (a) factoring the shared AST helpers (`_git_subcommand` global-option skipping, `_wrapper_name` forwarding, argv/list tracking, marker collection) into an importable module the oracle consumes, or (b) explicitly recording why the bare-discovery detector's semantics diverge enough from the write-seam lint that a separate implementation is warranted.

findings.checklist_item: Evaluate reusing scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py's AST detection machinery (argv tracking, _git wrapper resolution, _git_subcommand -C/--git-dir handling, synthetic self-tests) before building a second bespoke detector, and justify the new detector's novelty against it if reuse is rejected.

findings.checklist_item: Add a one-line positive rationale for the tree-derived static AST scan (e.g., it replaces the failed held-out oracle in place, keeps blast radius to the 2 offending files rather than flipping git config for the whole suite, and needs no per-test registration), so the mechanism choice is justified on its own merits.
evidence: The only rationale offered is negative/exclusionary: 'a new gate script would be a new ci_gate mechanism that check_mechanism_delta.py --check fails on' — this explains what to avoid, not why static AST identifier-matching is the right positive choice over, e.g., a runtime autouse conftest that executes the suite under safe.bareRepository=explicit
G6 checklist item 4: 'The plan states a POSITIVE rationale for the chosen approach (its absence is a finding)'
findings.finding: The plan gives no POSITIVE rationale for choosing a tree-derived static AST identifier-heuristic as the guard mechanism; it only argues against a scripts/check_*.py gate (a rejected-alternative note), leaving the fit of the chosen mechanism unjustified.
findings.location: Plan Step 2 (guard-mechanism paragraph, 'The guard stays a pytest oracle rather than a scripts/check_*.py wired into make lint')
scenarios: Implementer builds an elaborate AST idiom-enumeration detector without understanding why it was preferred, and cannot judge trade-offs when an idiom the enumeration missed appears
findings.suggested_fix: State that a static tree-wide AST oracle was chosen because it is surgical (fixes only the flagged sites), preserves the existing pytest-oracle ci_gate rather than introducing a new gate mechanism, and detects the banned construct without requiring the entire tests/ tree to already be portable — which a runtime safe.bareRepository=explicit conftest flip would demand.
